From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Threshold Points

1. **The "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "cleared by both sides" labels have no effect.** The cover note says these clauses are agreed and asks us to review only "[OPEN]" items. That is the Seller's framing, not an agreed position. Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN], so accepting the note would mean reviewing nothing. Every item below is reviewed on its merits. **Please check with your principals whether anything was actually agreed at principal level.** I cannot verify that claim, and the Seller's statement that it was is not evidence.
2. **The "market context" preamble is Seller advocacy.** It does not establish what is market for this deal.
3. **The Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark will be "addressed", and the incident is "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter says the Bluefen consent has not been obtained, the facility has not been repaid, and the incident's scope and notification position are unknown. Rely on the Disclosure Letter facts and use the inconsistency in negotiation.

---

## Issue-by-Issue Review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap, opening at 50% (AUD 12m) and landing no lower than 30–35%. The cap must apply only to general warranties. Fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Given the known risks (30% revenue customer, unresolved IP chain, live privacy incident), 20% is too thin. If the Seller holds firm, consider W&I insurance with a Seller retention.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), deductible, so only the excess is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **tipping** basket, so that once it is exceeded recovery runs from the first dollar.
  - Basket at about AUD 120,000 (0.5%) and de minimis at about AUD 10,000.
  - Related or recurring claims aggregated for the de minimis test.
  - Thresholds not to apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A deductible basket at about 1% plus a high de minimis materially erodes recovery. Without aggregation, related claims could be split to sit under AUD 25k each.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Also, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - At least 18–24 months for general warranties, covering at least one full audit cycle after Completion.
  - Tax claims: 5–7 years, outlasting the ATO amendment periods.
  - Title/capacity claims: 7 years (or the NSW statutory limitation period).
  - Specific indemnities: their own tailored periods.
  - Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Recommendation: Accept 18 months only for general warranties. Reject the catch-all.** The catch-all quietly imposes the 18-month bar on title, tax and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, issued capital) capped at 100% of price.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - A limitation period of at least 6–7 years.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** If title fails we have bought nothing, so recovery must match the full AUD 24m. "Simplicity" is not a reason to cap it at AUD 4.8m.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An express carve-out from *all* limitations (caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, buyer knowledge, exclusive remedy, non-reliance).
  - The carve-out to cover fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees and advisers.
  - Express preservation of claims for misleading or deceptive conduct where the conduct was fraudulent.
- **Recommendation: Insert. Non-negotiable.** As drafted, "of any nature" purports to limit fraud claims, and non-reliance language may be used to argue against any misleading-conduct claim.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 adds a broad non-admission.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Only matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter qualify warranties, meaning disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and quantum.
  - No general data room disclosure. At most, documents specifically referenced against a warranty.
  - Public records limited to named searches on a specified date.
  - Disclosure to have no effect against fundamental warranties, tax, or any specific indemnity.
  - DL 1.4 must not dilute any specific disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Reject general disclosure.** Combined with buyer knowledge (007), it would let the Seller defend almost any claim by pointing to something somewhere in the data room.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-buyer clause stating that the Buyer's knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, does not limit any claim except to the extent the matter was fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Fallback: *actual* knowledge of a short list of named deal-team individuals only, excluding advisers and constructive knowledge.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** "Discoverable" turns our due diligence into a waiver and makes the warranties largely illusory.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). The DL confirms no consent has been obtained and the cl 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **condition precedent** of Bluefen's unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - The consent not withdrawn at Completion.
  - All reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, Buyer involvement in approaching Bluefen, a long-stop date and a walk right.
  - Ideally, a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or adversely varies within 12 months because of the change of control.
- **Recommendation: Reject as drafted.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30% of revenue. "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions, and a conditional consent could leave the contract terminable.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release "to be provided following Completion". The DL confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at Completion** out of the price, treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free calculation.
  - A payoff letter before Completion.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, discharge of all security, and PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately).
  - Riverlark's cl 8.1 change-control consent or waiver if any period runs between signing and repayment.
  - Confirmation of whether the security includes a pledge over the sale shares (relevant to 015).
- **Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release.** If the release comes after Completion, we are paying for a business that is still encumbered and exposed to a change-of-control default.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The DL says it is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Bonuses plus all associated costs treated as Transaction Costs or debt-like items and deducted from the price. Associated costs include employer payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, PAYG withholding and any workers' comp on-costs.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The bonuses are a liability of the *Company*, which we will own. Leaving them out of the funds flow transfers at least AUD 420k, plus on-costs, to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). The DL says DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every fee, AUD 180k is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment, or the AUD 180k paid from the price or escrowed.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment, with moral rights consents, from Ironquay.
  - A specific indemnity covering failure of title to the SOW3 materials, third-party IP claims, and re-development or replacement cost.
  - That indemnity to sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits.
- **Recommendation: Reject as drafted.** Until the assignment is delivered the Company may not own the SOW3 IP. Indemnifying only the payment leaves the more serious ownership risk with us.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). The DL says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have gone to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification requirements are all unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment promptly. The Privacy Act NDB scheme expects assessment within 30 days, and depending on the incident date that may already be overdue.
  - The Seller to make any required OAIC and individual notifications, share the forensic report, and give the Buyer consultation rights.
  - A specific uncapped indemnity, or one capped separately at a meaningful level, for all losses. That includes regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, third-party claims and remediation.
  - The indemnity not to be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge, and outside thresholds and the general time limit.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure says scope and notifiability are unknown, so materiality cannot be assessed. Without an indemnity, disclosure would shift the whole risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The DL says they should be "read together" and is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of the renewals and their dates.
  - Confirmation of terms, termination rights, and amounts paid or accrued.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants requiring Buyer consent for commitments above a set threshold, measured on an aggregated basis for related contracts.
  - Any committed but unaccrued amount outside the ordinary course to be treated as a debt-like item, or covered by specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the label. Diligence it and aggregate.** Three identical related renewals, flagged by the Seller itself as linked, look like a split commitment. It should be tested against conduct-of-business thresholds rather than assumed to be ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Pre-categorised [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels. A single limitation regime applies to "all Claims" (cl 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5). Fundamental, tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit:
  - (a) General warranties
  - (b) Fundamental warranties
  - (c) Tax warranties and tax indemnity
  - (d) Specific indemnities: Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses, and Sandbar if needed
  - (e) Fraud, which is unlimited

  Default drafting should be that limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation: Reject the single regime and the labels.** Collapsing the categories is the main structural device in this draft. It turns a general-warranty cap of AUD 4.8m into the ceiling on everything.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The DL notes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent checks: ASIC company extract and historical searches reconciled to the register, the constitution, and the share certificates.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertibles, SAFEs, employee equity or pre-emptive rights.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company. Check whether Riverlark holds share security.
  - Fundamental title warranties as in 004.
  - Completion deliverables: executed transfers, certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), any waivers of pre-emptive rights, and releases of encumbrances.
- **Recommendation: Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** The Seller's register is the Seller's own record. Title must be verified externally and backed by an uncapped warranty.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity on a pound-for-pound basis, with no basket, capped at 100% of price and lasting 5–7 years, with conduct-of-claims rights.
  - If Paperbark is in Harbourglass's tax consolidated group: a valid tax sharing agreement, a tax funding agreement and a clear exit payment, so Paperbark is not exposed to group liabilities.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee and contractor assignments, and SaaS security. Give them a higher cap than general warranties and a longer period, linked to the Ironquay indemnity (011).
- **Recommendation: Treat as open.** These terms have not been negotiated. Leaving tax and IP in the 20%/18-month general regime is inappropriate for a SaaS target with a known IP-chain gap.

---

## Priority Summary

| Priority | Issues |
|---|---|
| **Must-win** | 004 Title regime; 005 Fraud; 006 Disclosure; 007 Buyer knowledge; 009 Riverlark; 014 Category separation |
| **High (specific risk)** | 008 Bluefen; 010 Bonuses; 011 Ironquay; 012 Privacy incident; 016 Tax/IP |
| **Negotiate** | 001 Cap; 002 Thresholds; 003 Time limits; 013 Sandbar; 015 Title verification (diligence) |

## Suggested Next Steps
1. Confirm with principals that no limitation package has been agreed, and tell Seller counsel the full draft remains open.
2. Ask for: the Bluefen cl 11.2/11.3 correspondence; a Riverlark payoff figure and security list; DD-005 bonus terms; Ironquay payment records; the DD-006 incident timeline and forensic status; the three Sandbar renewal contracts; and the ASIC and PPSR results.
3. Prepare the mark-up with separate liability schedules and adjust the funds flow for the facility, the bonuses and their on-costs, and the Ironquay payment.

*This analysis is for the Buyer deal team. Australian-specific points (NDB timing, tax consolidation, PPSR, payroll tax) should be confirmed by NSW-qualified counsel and tax advisers before being relied on.*

  - Ideally, a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or adversely varies within 12 months because of the change of control.
- **Recommendation: Reject as drafted.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30% of revenue. "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions, and a conditional consent could leave the contract terminable.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release "to be provided following Completion". The DL confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at Completion** out of the price, treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free calculation.
  - A payoff letter before Completion.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, discharge of all security, and PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately).
  - Riverlark's cl 8.1 change-control consent or waiver if any period runs between signing and repayment.
  - Confirmation of whether the security includes a pledge over the sale shares (relevant to 015).
- **Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release.** If the release comes after Completion, we are paying for a business that is still encumbered and exposed to a change-of-control default.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The DL says it is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Bonuses plus all associated costs treated as Transaction Costs or debt-like items and deducted from the price. Associated costs include employer payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, PAYG withholding and any workers' comp on-costs.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The bonuses are a liability of the *Company*, which we will own. Leaving them out of the funds flow transfers at least AUD 420k, plus on-costs, to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). The DL says DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every fee, AUD 180k is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment, or the AUD 180k paid from the price or escrowed.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment, with moral rights consents, from Ironquay.
  - A specific indemnity covering failure of title to the SOW3 materials, third-party IP claims, and re-development or replacement cost.
  - That indemnity to sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits.
- **Recommendation: Reject as drafted.** Until the assignment is delivered the Company may not own the SOW3 IP. Indemnifying only the payment leaves the more serious ownership risk with us.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). The DL says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have gone to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification requirements are all unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment promptly. The Privacy Act NDB scheme expects assessment within 30 days, and depending on the incident date that may already be overdue.
  - The Seller to make any required OAIC and individual notifications, share the forensic report, and give the Buyer consultation rights.
  - A specific uncapped indemnity, or one capped separately at a meaningful level, for all losses. That includes regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, third-party claims and remediation.
  - The indemnity not to be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge, and outside thresholds and the general time limit.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure says scope and notifiability are unknown, so materiality cannot be assessed. Without an indemnity, disclosure would shift the whole risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The DL says they should be "read together" and is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of the renewals and their dates.
  - Confirmation of terms, termination rights, and amounts paid or accrued.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants requiring Buyer consent for commitments above a set threshold, measured on an aggregated basis for related contracts.
  - Any committed but unaccrued amount outside the ordinary course to be treated as a debt-like item, or covered by specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the label. Diligence it and aggregate.** Three identical related renewals, flagged by the Seller itself as linked, look like a split commitment. It should be tested against conduct-of-business thresholds rather than assumed to be ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Pre-categorised [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels. A single limitation regime applies to "all Claims" (cl 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5). Fundamental, tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit:
  - (a) General warranties
  - (b) Fundamental warranties
  - (c) Tax warranties and tax indemnity
  - (d) Specific indemnities: Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses, and Sandbar if needed
  - (e) Fraud, which is unlimited

  Default drafting should be that limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation: Reject the single regime and the labels.** Collapsing the categories is the main structural device in this draft. It turns a general-warranty cap of AUD 4.8m into the ceiling on everything.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The DL notes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent checks: ASIC company extract and historical searches reconciled to the register, the constitution, and the share certificates.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertibles, SAFEs, employee equity or pre-emptive rights.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company. Check whether Riverlark holds share security.
  - Fundamental title warranties as in 004.
  - Completion deliverables: executed transfers, certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), any waivers of pre-emptive rights, and releases of encumbrances.
- **Recommendation: Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** The Seller's register is the Seller's own record. Title must be verified externally and backed by an uncapped warranty.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity on a pound-for-pound basis, with no basket, capped at 100% of price and lasting 5–7 years, with conduct-of-claims rights.
  - If Paperbark is in Harbourglass's tax consolidated group: a valid tax sharing agreement, a tax funding agreement and a clear exit payment, so Paperbark is not exposed to group liabilities.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee and contractor assignments, and SaaS security. Give them a higher cap than general warranties and a longer period, linked to the Ironquay indemnity (011).
- **Recommendation: Treat as open.** These terms have not been negotiated. Leaving tax and IP in the 20%/18-month general regime is inappropriate for a SaaS target with a known IP-chain gap.
